overview.description: Dreierles (also known as Dreierle or Dreier) is a sophisticated trick-taking game from the Baden region of Germany, played with a 54-card Cego (Tarot) deck. It belongs to the Tarock family and is closely related to Austrian Tapp Tarock. In Dreierles, a single declarer plays against a team of opponents, utilizing a six-card 'blind' (talon) from which they draw exactly three cards to improve their hand, giving the game its name.

history.origins: Dreierles survived as a niche tradition in central Baden (around Rastatt) alongside the better known Cego. It likely shares an ancestor with 19th-century Austrian Tarock variants, possibly imported during the era of the Austrian garrisons in the Rastatt federal fortress.
timeline: 1820s: Early forms of Tapp Tarock emerge in Central Europe.
1850s: Tarock games become established in the Baden military and social clubs.
Modern Era: Maintained by dedicated groups in Steinmauern and the Achertal region.
history.evolution: While Cego became the 'national game' of Baden, Dreierles preserved a more traditional Tarock structure with fewer contracts and a fixed three-card draw mechanic.
history.cultural: Played in traditional 'GasthÃ¶fe' (inns) and family circles; it is one of the few surviving German card games to use a full 54ndcard Tarot deck.

setup.players: Usually 3 players. If 4 play, the dealer sits out the hand.
setup.deck: 54-card Cego pack. Consists of 22 Tarocks (Trumps), 16 Court cards (K, Q, C, J), and 16 pip cards (Leere).
setup.dealing: Each player receives 16 cards (in batches of 4). 6 cards are dealt face-down to the center to form the 'Blind' (Talon).

rules.objective: Score more than 35 points (out of 70 total) for the declarer, or prevent the declarer from doing so for the defenders.
rules.gameplay:
1. Bidding: Players bid for the right to be the declarer. The highest bid wins.
2. The Draw: The declarer takes any 3 cards from the 6-card blind and discards 3 non-scoring cards (Leere) in their place.
3. Trick Play: Standard Tarock rules. Trumps (Tarocks) always win against suit cards. You MUST follow suit or play a trump if void.
keyRules: Red suits (Hearts/Diamonds) rank: King (High), Queen, Cavalier, Jack, 1, 2, 3, 4 (Low).
Black suits (Spades/Clubs) rank: King (High), Queen, Cavalier, Jack, 10, 9, 8, 7 (Low).
The GstieÃŸ (Fool) is the highest trump.
Pfeife (trump 1) bonus: if the declarer wins the last trick with the Pfeife, they receive extra game points from each opponent; if it loses, they pay.

strategy.basic: As declarer, use the 3ndcard draw to complete your trump sequences or to 'void' a suit so you can trump in later.
strategy.intermediate: Teamwork: Defenders must work together to 'bleed' the declarer's trumps using their long suits.
strategy.advanced: The Pagat Ultimo: Keeping the Tarock 1 until the very last trick requires impeccable card counting and timing, as it is easily lost if trumps are led early.
tips: Keep track of the SkÃ¼s (GstieÃŸ) and the 21; they are the only cards that can beat a high Tarock.
Remember the reverse ranking in red suitsâ€”it is a common beginner mistake to lose a high red card to a lower number.

list.description: Solo Du bid (win all 16 tricks, no blind); scoring as positive/negative points; Kleiner Mann am Schluss; Ramsch for all-pass; 4 active players get 12 cards each.

difficulty.easy: Doesn't understand reverse red-suit ranking; misses Pagat bonuses.
difficulty.medium: Strategic draw selection from the blind; coordinated defense with partner.
difficulty.hard: Perfect point-tracking; calculates the optimal discard to maximize trump utility.

considerations: AI needs a specialized module for Cego-deck point values (which differ from standard 52ndcard decks).

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: Tarocks 1-21 plus Stiess (highest); outrank suit cards.
trumpConfig.overtakingRule: No obligation to beat; highest trump in trick wins, else highest of led suit.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Declarer leads to first trick; thereafter trick winner leads.

edgeCases.text: If all three players pass in bidding, a Räuber is played: no blind used, player taking most card points loses.
Misdeal: cards redealt by same dealer.
Incorrect discard or illegal play: play ends; offender pays 4 game points × bid factor × knock doubles. Revoke may be corrected before next card played without penalty.

engine.deckDescription: A 54-card Cego-family tarock pack with 21 numbered trumps plus the Fool and 32 French-suited cards, using the same reduced suit structure as the Austrian 54-card tarock deck.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits split into black and red colour groups, with different reduced pip sequences beneath the courts.
engine.rankDescription: Black suits keep 10, 9, 8, 7 under King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack; red suits keep Ace, 2, 3, 4 under the same courts. Trumps run from 1 to 21 plus the Fool.
engine.dealPattern: 6 cards face-down to centre as blind; remainder in batches of 8 (or 4+4) to each player starting to dealer's right; each receives 16 cards.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: Declarer takes cards from the blind in a one-time exchange after bidding; there is no draw-from-stock during trick play.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Declarer discards only during the exchange phase (equal to number drawn from blind); no discard during trick play.
